plan: My value is $19, high in the $0-$20 range. To maximize profit, I should bid slightly below my value to ensure a win while minimizing cost. Assume Betty and Charles bid randomly up to $20; a bid of $18.9 is aggressive enough to win against most bids, but low enough to ensure profit if I win. This strategy considers the possibility of others bidding close to their value, maximizing my chance of winning and profit.

Given my value of $24, I should aim to bid just above the expected second-highest bid to maximize profit. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0 and $20, the expected second-highest bid could be around $13. To ensure a win, I will bid slightly higher than this expectation, at $13.1, to maximize my profit margin. This strategy minimizes payment while securing the prize.

Given my value of $21, I should aim to bid slightly above the average expected value of the other bidders to maximize profit. Since values are drawn uniformly between $0 and $20, the average value is $10. I will bid slightly above this to ensure a win, but not so much that it significantly reduces my profit. A bid of $15 balances winning likelihood and profit.
